operator: Washington State Ferries, a division of the Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT)
jurisdiction: Washington State, USA — Puget Sound & the San Juan Islands

authority_profile.scale: Largest ferry system in the United States — ~24 million riders/year, 10 routes, 20 terminals; part of the state highway system.
authority_profile.mandate: Essential public mobility across Puget Sound and the San Juan Islands; auto- and passenger-ferry backbone under WSDOT.

decarbonization_anchor: WSF is executing a fleet-wide hybrid-electric conversion and new-build program with shore-charging infrastructure, under Washington's legislated climate commitments (Climate Commitment Act) and the state's net-zero direction. A zero-emission passenger-only foiling tier is an additive complement to the auto-ferry electrification program.
domestic_first_note: Leads entirely with the domestic Puget Sound / San Juan Islands network built on WSF's live terminals and published network plan. No cross-border corridors.
hazards: Puget Sound is sheltered home water but has strong tidal currents in the passes (Deception Pass, San Juan channels) — route hand-waypoints must respect current and traffic separation schemes.
Heavy commercial and naval traffic near the Seattle waterfront and Bremerton (Puget Sound Naval Shipyard) — corridors keep clear of restricted naval zones.
The foiling tier is passenger-only and additive; it does not replace the auto-ferry backbone that carries vehicles and freight.
positioning: Passenger-only, zero-emission foiling layer above the auto-ferry backbone: fast, frequent, low-wake hops on the busy Seattle-side commuter channels (Bainbridge, Bremerton, Kingston, Vashon), complementing the electrifying auto fleet and opening frequencies the big auto boats can't run economically.
